# Facilities inventory lookup

A shared per-key query cache provides subscribe(key,options) -> unique observer
handle, unsubscribe(handle), online(boolean), focus(boolean), snapshot(key),
and dispose() of observer scopes. Queries retain status (pending/success/error),
fetchStatus (idle/fetching/paused), and data. queryFn receives a lazy signal
accessor. Each actual access records consumption; each fetch owns its controller
and completion. Completion is asynchronous; initial online entry is synchronous,
paused continuation resumes on a Promise turn. First start uses network mode;
continuation also needs focus. 'always' can run offline; 'offlineFirst' allows
first offline entry but retry can pause. Retries use explicit scheduler handles.
Multiple observers share one fetch. Unconsumed active work can finish into cache
after its view departs; consumed work is physically abortable. Cancellation
reverts previous query data/status and settles the originating attempt. Late
fulfillment cannot become a new attempt's data. Unknown unsubscribe is inert.
The component owns observer scope; the cache remains outside individual views.
Dependency versions and build/test configuration are outside the repair scope.

Embedding API: bind registers a native callable; Environment.call
provides newAttempt(key,number), abort(key,number), request(key,number, lazy-read
token, completion token), defer(callback token), schedule(callback token,delay).
The request host calls queryFn with an actual AbortSignal property. Reading it
invokes the native consumption closure synchronously; Promise settlement later
invokes the native completion with {ok,value}. All observer, retry, cancellation,
state and cache logic executes in the target language. No native JS Promise or
DOM claim is made. Native object identity binds query and attempt generations;
wire handles only identify injected callbacks. 
Element-owned subscriptions and namespaced event ingress; persistent external cache

export function mount(session,element){const node=$(element);node.data('queryClient',session);session.project=q=>node.text(q.key+':'+q.state.status+':'+q.state.fetchStatus);node.text('empty');for(const command of ['subscribe','unsubscribe','online','focus'])node.on(command+'.lookup',(_,args)=>node.data('queryClient')[command](...args));return {subscribe:(k,o)=>node.triggerHandler('subscribe.lookup',[[k,o]]),unsubscribe:h=>node.triggerHandler('unsubscribe.lookup',[[h]]),online:v=>node.triggerHandler('online.lookup',[[v]]),focus:v=>node.triggerHandler('focus.lookup',[[v]]),snapshot:k=>session.snapshot(k),dispose(){session.dispose();node.off('.lookup');node.removeData('queryClient');}};}

checkpoints: Subscribe a fresh key with default/online network mode while offline and confirm no queryFn invocation occurs immediately.
Unsubscribe its only observer before reconnect, reconnect, and confirm queryFn is still never invoked.
Repeat with a signal-consuming queryFn and confirm no live AbortSignal is delivered after reconnect.
Verify the result is unchanged when refetchOnReconnect is absent, false, or true, insofar as that option is accepted by the existing interface.
Verify an observed paused initial query still resumes on a Promise turn once online and focused.
Verify multiple observers continue to share one fetch and removing only one observer does not abandon work needed by remaining observers.
Verify consumed in-flight work is aborted and late completion cannot update a newer attempt.
Run the public syntax/build checks without changing tests, dependencies, or build configuration.
forbidden_effects: Do not invoke the queryFn for an observerless fresh online-mode attempt that was mounted and unmounted entirely offline.
Do not expose a live AbortSignal from that abandoned attempt after reconnect.
Do not make refetchOnReconnect control the required abandonment behavior.
Do not cancel unconsumed work that has already started merely because its last view departs; it may finish into the cache.
Do not allow completion from an old or cancelled attempt to become a newer attempt's data.
Do not make unknown unsubscribe handles mutate query state.
Do not dispose the external cache merely because an individual view or component is disposed.
Do not change dependencies, tests, interfaces, or build/test configuration.
lifecycle_identity: A query is identified by its cache key and native query object identity.
Each fetch attempt has a distinct generation/number, controller, settlement state, and completion.
Observer handles are unique subscriptions and are distinct from query and attempt identity.
A late callback is valid only for the same current, unsettled attempt; reuse of a key does not make an old attempt current.
Component/view lifetime owns observer scope, while cache lifetime remains external to individual views.

obligations.text: A fresh default online-mode query subscribed while offline must remain paused and must not invoke queryFn until it becomes eligible.
If that fresh paused query loses its final observer before reconnect, the originating attempt must be abandoned or settled so reconnect cannot invoke its queryFn or provide it a live signal.
The behavior in O2 must hold independently of refetchOnReconnect.
A paused attempt that still has an observer may resume asynchronously on a Promise turn when both connectivity and focus make it eligible.

Network-mode behavior must remain supported: always may start offline; offlineFirst may enter initially while offline but may pause a retry; default online mode requires connectivity for first start; continuation additionally requires focus.
Multiple observers of one key must continue sharing one fetch, and removing one observer must not abandon an attempt while other observers remain.
Signal consumption must remain lazy and synchronous on property access; consumed active work must remain physically abortable.

Unconsumed work that has actually started may complete into the cache after its view departs, while cancellation must restore the prior data/status, set fetchStatus idle, and settle its originating attempt.

Success, failure, retry, resume, and other asynchronous callbacks must update state only when their originating attempt is still the current unsettled attempt; late fulfillment must not supply a newer attempt's data.
Unknown unsubscribe must remain inert, observer-scope disposal must preserve the external cache, and the existing public API, dependencies, and build/test configuration must remain unchanged.

ordering_barriers: Initial eligible entry is synchronous, but a paused continuation must cross a Promise-turn boundary before invoking queryFn.
Final-observer removal for a never-started paused attempt must invalidate or settle that attempt before any later online/focus resume callback can invoke it.
Signal consumption is recorded synchronously when queryFn reads the lazy signal property, before later Promise settlement.
Cancellation must mark the originating attempt settled and restore prior state before abort-triggered or ordinary late completion can project data.
Retry-delay callbacks and queued resume callbacks must revalidate current attempt identity and settlement before invoking or updating state.

Preserve synchronous initial online entry and Promise-turn resumption of paused continuation.
Preserve network modes online, always, and offlineFirst, including focus requirements for continuation.
Preserve explicit scheduler-based retries and the existing retry/retryDelay behavior except where an observerless never-started attempt must not resume.
Preserve fetch sharing across multiple observers.
Preserve lazy signal access, per-fetch controllers, physical abort for consumed work, and completion ownership.
Preserve completion of already-started unconsumed work into the cache after view departure.
Preserve cancellation rollback and stale-completion isolation.
Preserve inert unknown unsubscribe, element-owned subscriptions, namespaced event ingress, and externally persistent cache lifetime.
Preserve dependencies and build/test configuration.

active(q,a){return q.attempt===a&&!a.settled;}
if(q.observers.size===0){const a=q.attempt;if(a&&!a.settled){if(q.consumed)this.cancel(q,a);else a.retryCancelled=true;}}

resume(q){const a=q.attempt;if(a&&this.active(q,a)&&q.state.fetchStatus==='paused'&&this.eligible(a)&&!a.queued){a.queued=true;Promise.resolve().then(()=>{a.queued=false;if(!this.active(q,a))return;if(a.failures&&a.retryCancelled){a.settled=true;q.state={...q.state,status:'error',fetchStatus:'idle'};this.project(q);return;}this.invoke(q,a);});}}

Success, failure, retry, resume, and other asynchronous callbacks must update state only when their originating attempt is still the current unsettled attempt; late fulfillment must not supply a newer attempt's data.
